# The Witness of the Wanderers

## Scripture
"Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him." — Matthew 2:2

## Reflection
Long before GPS or compasses, travelers looked to the wandering stars—the planets that drift slowly against the fixed constellations. Ancient astronomers noticed these "wanderers" traced patterns across the night sky, and one such celestial sign led the Magi on a journey of faith, seeking the newborn King.

In September evenings, look low on the eastern horizon after twilight. Jupiter rises, a steady beacon moving through the stars, reminding us that God sometimes guides us not through sudden revelations but through quiet, patient movement—signs that unfold over weeks and months.

The Magi didn't have all the answers. They saw, they trusted, they journeyed. Their story reminds us that faith often means following light we don't fully understand yet. God still speaks through creation, still sets signs in the heavens, still draws seekers toward Himself.

Perhaps you're in a season of seeking, uncertain where the path leads. Take heart: the same God who guided stargazers from the East guides you. He doesn't always reveal the destination, but He always provides enough light for the next step.

## Prayer
Lord of the heavens, thank You for the signs You place in creation that draw us toward You. When we cannot see the whole path, give us courage to follow the light You provide. Like the Magi, may we journey faithfully, trusting that every step of seeking leads us closer to Your heart. Amen.
